newsitem.title: USA: US Gulf Coast lures Brent crude, W African scant.
newsitem.headline: US Gulf Coast lures Brent crude, W African scant.

text.p: The U.S. Gulf Coast lured fresh offers for North Sea Brent crude on Monday, reflecting attractive transatlantic economics, traders said on Monday.
A major trading house was offering one million barrels of Brent crude for May 8-12 delivery, asking for a discount of 70-80 cents to benchmark West Texas Intermediate/Cushing.
A European major that completed the sale of five Brent cargoes into the Louisiana Offshore Oil Port (LOOP) last week was mulling bringing over another batch, traders said.
The spread between WTI and Brent was around $1.70-75 a barrel on Monday afternoon, encouraging the transatlantic flow.
Among other UK crudes, a U.S. refiner was offering onshore crude Wyche Farm for June WTI/Cushing minus 60 cents a barrel delivered around May 18-22, traders said.
Two Oseberg cargoes for mid-May arrival were still looking for homes around June WTI minus 70-80 cents a barrel.
West African pickings have slimmed over the past week, particularly among heavy sweets such as Cabinda, as a result of renewed Asian and Mediterranean buying.
A U.S. company was offering Angolan Palanca crude for end-May arrival, asking June WTI/Cushing minus 40 cents a barrel.

A Gulf Coast buyer suggested that inexpensive West African crudes have eclipsed North Sea crudes in recent weeks. "West African crudes have been making it difficult for North Sea barrels to win," he said.
Meanwhile, as May activity winds down, traders were still abuzz over signs that ARCO might deliver Bonny Light crude into the NYMEX upon expiry of the May contract on Tuesday.

Exchange for Physicals (EFPs) have been commanding a premium of six to 12 cents a barrel over the past few weeks as traders rush to escape paper positions that might leave them with a grade other than WTI.
ARCO was heard to have already moved some two million barrels of the Nigerian crude into Cushing in anticipation of a delivery. Company officials declined to comment.
In Latin America, Uruguay's state oil refiner ANCAP is seeking to buy one million barrels of crude oil for delivery June 20-25, trade sources said.
Bids will be received through April 28. ANCAP will award the tender on April 29.
As in previous tenders, the company is seeking to purchase crude with an API gravity of 26-45 degrees and a sulfur content of 0.5 percent to 1.8 percent.
Uruguay's 34,600 barrel per day (bpd) La Teja refinery is expected to be fully operational by the beginning of May after the catalytic cracker was replaced, sources said.
